sentences.text: Neuquensuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform that lived during the Santonian age of the Upper Cretaceous in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
This small animal had upper arm bones measuring about 10.0 centimeters, a thigh bone about 9.4 centimeters, and a shin bone about 10.5 centimeters long.
Neuquensuchus had a shin longer than its thigh, a trait suggesting it possessed some running ability unlike most other crocodyliforms.
Its shin was longer than its femur, a condition shared only with Shantungosuchus among known crocodyliforms with measurable leg bones.
Fossil evidence suggests it was a swift, land-living animal with limb proportions well-suited for running.
The fossils of Neuquensuchus were discovered on the campus of the Universidad Nacional del Comahue in the city of Neuquén.
Neuquensuchus was named by Lucas E. Fiorelli and Jorge O. Calvo in 2007, with the publication becoming available in 2008.
While later analyses placed Neuquensuchus in the notosuchian clade Ziphosuchia, an analysis by Gabriel Liu and colleagues in 2017 upheld its original classification.
Neuquensuchus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
